The orphan-markdown validator explicitly exempts exploration.md.
Other manifest validation and unlisted-markdown rejection remain intact.
ExploreRequested reads the set-level explore boolean.
Only explicit true enables automatic exploration; absent, false and malformed values do not.
ExplorerOverride reads agents and effort through the shared AgentDirective parser.
The authoring guide documents both keys and explicitly contrasts opt-in exploration with opt-out verification and refinement.
The guide states the shared-seam dependency rule for two or more AFK tasks.
Shared constants supply key and file names, with a guide-to-manifest drift test.
The explore command invokes a fresh agent with the manifest listing, all task bodies and available spec.
The explorer template requests locations, ownership, invariants, test structure and file ranges.
The template requires anchored claims, approximately one page and the observed tree.
Neither the explorer instructions nor report framing introduces a prior-art section.
Successful exploration writes directly to the flat exploration.md path, replacing existing content.
Explore has its own captured-run phase, spend bucket and phase-labelled retry-cap accounting.
Manual exploration bypasses both manifest participation and the machine-wide enabled gate.
Failed, timed-out and interrupted agent attempts cannot reach report writing.
Command integration tests exercise agent replies, report replacement and the captured Explore stream row.
Implement prompts conditionally include the report path and explain its purpose.
Implement prompt construction checks report presence and supplies only its path.
The prompt permits corrections only where the current attempt falsified a line.
The edit boundary explicitly allows the exploration report beside the task file.
The existing “Before you hand-write mechanism” block remains unchanged.
Assist prompts include the exploration pointer beside refinement and recent progress.
Implement and assist golden fixtures cover report-present and report-absent cases.
The drain invokes explorePhase before its first task selection.
An existing report immediately bypasses the explorer and its spending.
Undeclared sets bypass automatic exploration.
The dedicated work.explore group defaults enabled when its group or enabled key is absent.
The configuration gate suppresses automatic passes while manual exploration remains available.
Agent and effort resolution follows CLI overrides, manifest explorer, then configuration.
explorePhase explicitly skips human-completed sets.
Report presence controls reuse; no checkout-to-report SHA freshness comparison occurs.
Whole-drain tests assert explorer execution without a report and no execution with an existing report.
Exploration uses the shared fallback walker with the standard retry cap and delays.
Exhausted exploration derives EXPLORE-FAILED and stops the drain before implementation.
Parking derives from captured-run metadata and report absence without schema changes.
EXPLORE-FAILED is separate from BLOCKED, whose derivation remains unchanged.
Daemon dispatch and automatic READY selection exclude the overlaid EXPLORE-FAILED status.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status, so a parked set with an eligible HITL task remains selectable.
Failed manual exploration can park a declared set without a progress record; only the drain’s explorePhase appends one.
The forwarded --skip-explore flag bypasses exploration and allows a parked set’s tasks to drain.
Writing a report or removing the explore declaration clears the derived park.
CONTEXT.md names EXPLORE-FAILED as a drain stop and an automatic-selection exclusion.
Unexplored sets carry a separate mark with the reason rendered in detail.
ResolveExploreMark returns no mark for sets that never requested exploration.
Shared read-side resolution populates rows consumed by dashboard, detail and status surfaces.
Containers retain the exploration mark, and shared status-cell rendering displays it on parked rows.
The dashboard exploration section renders the report path and recorded tree without its body.
The sign-off gate includes exploration beside refinement in its preamble and report-reading menu.
A missing report after a successful run is classified as pass-failed, parking the set instead of regenerating the report.

scores.rationale: Shared machinery and broad integration coverage support maintainability, but parking logic mishandles report deletion, HITL fallback and manual-failure progress records.

rows.title: The report is an artifact, and a set can ask for exploration
A builder reads the report and corrects what it falsified
A drain explores before it implements
A set that cannot be explored parks
The mark says whether a set was explored
